kind: independent read-only semantic review of frozen CI follow-up
excluded: Changing evidence/producer_runtime.py helper implementation was not reviewed.

findings.title: Preserve the first normally returned cleanup problem before later successful recovery clears it
findings.detail: The normal recovery path accepts a nonempty problems list from stop_registered, verify_stopped or cleanup_directories and stores only mutable recovery_problem. A later successful recovery clears that field to None. first_recovery_failure is added only in the thrown-exception branch, so normally returned cleanup failures lose their original diagnostic history after cleanup succeeds.
findings.impact: Diagnostic-history preservation gap. The new pre-cleanup accounting order still preserves incomplete status, observed charge floor and full reservation; this probe does not show an accounting or acceptance bypass.
findings.reproduction: Compile only the actual runtime.update lambda from line443 as a pure AST fragment. Apply it to an in-memory record first with problems=[original returned cleanup error], then with problems=[]. The first record is stopping/recovery_problem set; the second is terminal/recovery_problem None, with no first_recovery_failure.
findings.recommended_fix: When the normal problems list is nonempty, save the first bounded failure observation with setdefault using the same original-preservation semantics as thrown errors; add a returned-error-then-success regression.
findings.status: Reported to root; fix/recheck not yet included in this report.

review_conclusions.conclusion: After verified guardian/owner disappearance and recovery-claim acquisition, pending uncertainty and run incomplete status are durably recorded before stop/verify/directory cleanup begins. Therefore a later cleanup exception cannot leave the run active merely because cleanup failed before the old accounting step.

Recovery does not settle/cancel pending producer reservations. record_uncertain receives the same original observed floor; accounting owner remains responsible for idempotent max-floor updates. New tests assert original gross 230 bytes/3 files, complete 65536-byte/20-file/local hold, unchanged raw bytes and original session fields across repeats, successful eventual cleanup and unsafe retry rejection.

Thrown expected cleanup errors produce retained/incomplete actions, status stopping and first_recovery_failure through setdefault; later healthy cleanup clears only current recovery_problem. Claim release is in finally. Unavailable diagnostic persistence is reported explicitly rather than presented as saved history.

Fixture performs an actual rename/recreate through a cleanup callback only after verify_stopped returns no errors and real registered cleanup completes. It asserts callback execution, distinct replacement identity, preserved original directory identity and original bytes. It then requires explicit final identity-change failure, incomplete final proof and full pending reservation. This is a legitimate post-exit replacement exercise without assuming Windows allows moving an open output root.

review_conclusions.area: lost guardian and coordinator workflow fixture
review_conclusions.conclusion: Fallback barrier preserves real startup recovery but holds the coordinator immediately before its second applied recovery. Parent verifies live coordinator identity and barrier phase/count before deliberately losing the coordinator, so the double-owner-loss test cannot accidentally pass through prior coordinator recovery. A separate surviving-coordinator test exercises real unmodified fallback and validates no successful result artifact, failed run, full hold and blocked retry. Timeout allowance remains finite and actual timeout assertions remain.
New diagnostic extracts only the requested attempt action and limited problem fields, with finite string bounds; unrelated action context is excluded. It is not a product acceptance result.
